chapter_theme: The catalogue of shrines (க்ஷேத்திரக் கோவை): a single song that strings together the names of Siva's and Murugan's shrines across the Tamil country, from Kumbakonam, Arur and Chidambaram to Senthil, Eragam, Avinankudi and Vayalur, and ends with Murugan dwelling in every temple in the world.
structure_note: One song with no plea: the whole first and second halves are a list of places, each line ending in an address to Murugan (வாழ்வே, செகநாதம், வருதேவே, வயலூரா, மணிமார்பா), closing on the goddesses who praise him and his two consorts.

1306.reading: The song is a garland of shrine names: Kumbakonam, Arur, Chidambaram, Sirkazhi, Mayuram, Sivakasi, Rameswaram where the Veda-knowing one came alone to worship, Evvulur, Parangiri, Thiruvadanai, Senthil, Edakam, Solaimalai, Eragam, Avinankudi, the hills one by one, Virinjai, Kanchi, Vayalur, Perur, Kandiyur and others, each a place where Murugan lives. It closes with the women who contend with Siva, Vani, Lakshmi and the beautiful one, praising him every day, and with Murugan who married Indrani's daughter and the hunter girl, the lord in every temple throughout the world.
1306.nuance: The song has no confession: its devotion is the naming of places, and the last line (உலகெங்கு மேவிய தேவாலயந்தொறு பெருமாளே) turns the list into a claim that the Lord is in every temple, not only these. குன்று தோறுடன் echoes the 'every hill' (குன்றுதோறாடல்) of Murugan's worship. Several names are hard to identify because the rhythm splits them (செம்பு கேசுரம், செங்சோ லேரகம், கம்பை மாவடி, தென்சி வாயமு), and the reading of these is tentative.

source_issues: 1306: corrupt glyph ஧ in ஧வ்ளுர் (probably எவ்வுளூர், Tiruvallur), and ஡ in வயலு஡ரா, read வயலூரா (flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS: 2).
1306: செங்சோ லேரக looks corrupt (perhaps செங்கோடு, ஏரகம்); a stray space after உ splits உம்பர் at two line starts.
